Commentary.Commentary: We are back with India's reply! The umpires and players are all out in the middle. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the openers for India Women! Fatima Sana Khan has the new ball in hand and is raring to go! Let's play says the umpire.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the total of 105 does not look to be enough and Pakistan will have to bowl really well if they are to defend this. India on the other hand, will back themselves to chase it down and if they get an opportunity, could try to improve their net run rate which took a beating in the first game. Second half in a bit.

Shreyanka Patil is in for a chat. She says it’s special to get her first wicket in a World Cup. Mentions it is special to be a part of the World Cup, she’s always cheered for India but she feels good now people are cheering for her. Credits the bowlers for the way they bowled and she backs her side to chase it down.

The going was majorly slow for Pakistan. Whenever they looked to up the ante, they ended up losing a wicket. At one stage, they were in big trouble at 52 for 5. Nida Dar though, like she has done so many times in her career, came to the rescue and her stand with Syeda Aroob Shah has given their side's score some respectability.

That’s a fine effort from the ball by the Indians. Had all their chances been taken, it would have been a better effort but they’ll be very pleased after being asked to take the field. Their bowlers were on the money right from the word go. Renuka Singh Thakur and Deepti Sharma were excellent in the Powerplay. Arundhati Reddy and Shreyanka Patil then continued the good work and ended up being the pick of the bowlers. They hardly gave any runs away and got crucial wickets too. Asha Sobhana dropped a couple of catches and wasn't at her best with the ball but she was decent.

FOUR! Nashra Sundhu gets it through and Pakistan Women end their inning with a boundary! Arundhati Reddy keeps it full and just outside off, Nashra Sundhu crouches low and hits it straight over the bowler's head with an angled bat. The ball races away and beats the diving Shreyanka Patil, at long on to her left despite a full stretched dive. Pakistan Women end at 105/8!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! India have capitalized on the slow nature of the pitch and find themselves in a commanding position at the halfway mark of the innings, having claimed four wickets. In contrast, Pakistan Women have faced difficulties navigating the conditions and a significant responsibility now rests on this batting pair to weather the storm, forge a partnership, and steer their team out of trouble. Meanwhile, India will be eager to maintain their momentum, pressing forward to seize more wickets and tighten their grip on the game. Renuka Singh Thakur (2-0-13-1) will bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: How did that miss the stumps? Pushed through by Patil, on a nagging length, over middle, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi gets across a bit too far to sweep it fine on the leg side. Does not manage to make any contact but the extra bounce off the surface helps her as the ball goes over the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up nicely, full and on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi skips down the track and goes inside out. Clears the in-field as she gets it over cover for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from around the wicket and bowls it full, on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi pats it to the right of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Shreyanka Patil to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shreyanka Patil comes into the attack now.
Slows it up and bowls it a bit shorter in length, outside off, Omaima Sohail waits for the ball but decides to let it go through to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Deepti Sharma to Omaima Sohail, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Omaima Sohail walks out to bat at number 4 for Pakistan Women!

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Deepti slows it up and pulls the length back a bit, on middle and leg, Sidra Amin goes for the sweep again but does not manage to get any bat on it this time. The ball comes off her body and trickles onto the leg stump, dislodging the left bail. Sidra Amin is livid with herself. India Women have their second and Pakistan Women are now 25/2.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, OUT! b Deepti Sharma.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Sidra Amin gets it away! Pushed through by Deepti, full and on off, Sidra Amin walks across her stumps and brings out the sweep. Hits it to the left of short fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and fuller, on middle, Sidra Amin sweeps it straight to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Has Sidra Amin paid the price for being a bit casual? Very full from Deepti, on middle, Sidra Amin gets her bat down in time and jams it out to the left of the bowler. The ball bounces off the turf to the left of the bowler. Deepti sticks out her left and snaffles it. Turns around and fires in a throw at the batting end. Sidra had stepped out while playing her shot and had to quickly plonk her bat inside the crease. The throw hits and the third umpire is called into action. The replays show that Sidra managed to get her bat inside the crease in time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slower and shorter, on off, Sidra Amin hops and frees her arms to cut this one away. Ends up chopping it down on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: THREE WIDES! Wayward from Deepti! Spills this one down leg, on a length, Sidra Amin goes for the sweep but misses. The keeper, Richa Ghosh moves to her left but fails to cut it off. The ball gets past her for a couple of runs more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, 3 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Change of ends for Deepti Sharma!

That stayed low! Angled across the left-hander from over the wicket, on a back of a length, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi stays put and tries to drag this one on the leg side. The ball stays low and scoots under her bat. A good take by the keeper standing up to the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Half a shout for LBW but the impact looked outside off there! Reddy hurls it full and on the off-stump line, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi walks across a bit and goes for a swipe across the line. The ball goes under her bat and she wears it near the knee roll on the front pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: From around the wicket for the left-hander, on a length, around off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi hangs on the back foot and stabs it down on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Arundhati Reddy to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling in, on a good length, Sidra Amin gets down for the sweep but a bit of extra bounce results in the ball coming off her right bicep and rolls in front of short third for a leg bye. There is a direct hit at the batting end but Muneeba Ali Siddiqi was well in.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Arundhati Reddy to Sidra Amin, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Missed out! Strays on the pads does Reddy, on a fuller length, Sidra Amin glances it off her pads but picks out the fielder at short fine leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Arundhati Reddy to Sidra Amin, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Uppish but Sidra gets away with it! Reddy begins from over the wicket and bowls it full, around off, Sidra Amin goes through her shot early as she tries to go back over the bowler's head. Chips it on the bounce to the fielder at mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Arundhati Reddy to Sidra Amin, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arundhati Reddy is introduced into the attack.

FOUR! Does not get hold of it but enough to clear mid off! Renuka serves a bit too full, on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi gets underneath it, clears her front leg and tonks it back over the bowler's head. Gets this one from the toe end of the bat but still manages to clear the leaping Harmanpreet Kaur at mid off for a boundary. A good over for Pakistan. 12 runs off it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Renuka changes her angle of attack as she comes from around the wicket and angles it into the left-hander, full and on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi walks across her stumps and brings her bottom hand into play. Firms the drive but can't get it past Shafali Verma at mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Serves it full and on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi gets on the front foot and knocks it along the ground to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: THREE WIDES! Renuka errs in line as she drifts down leg, on a length, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi misses the tickle and it goes past the right thigh of the keeper, Richa Ghosh. The ball rolls down towards the deep fine leg fence for a couple of runs. Given as wides by the umpire but the replays show that it came off the thigh pad of Muneeba.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, 3 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: A tighter line this time from Renuka, fuller and on the off-stump line, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi eases the drive with a straight bat to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Angling across the batter, on a length, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi gets the width she needs. Frees her arms and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Shaping in from over the wicket, full and on middle, despite the keeper being upto the stumps, Sidra Amin steps out and manages to get just enough bat on it to get it down to deep fine leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Renuka Singh Thakur to Sidra Amin, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Keeps it short on a flatter trajectory, on middle, Sidra Amin hangs back and pulls it aerially but well in front of deep square leg for another single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Deepti bowls it flat and short, attacking the stumps, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi hops back and gets inside the line of the ball. Whips it off her pads to the left of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This goes across the batter from over the wicket, full and on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi pushes it off the front foot to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through slightly, fuller and on off, Sidra Amin brings out the sweep and hits it in front of square on the leg side. Gets off the mark with a single does Amin.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Deepti Sharma to Sidra Amin, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up by Deepti, full and on off, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi gets down and sweeps it to the left of deep square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Deepti starts off on a nagging length, on middle and leg, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi presses half-forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Deepti Sharma to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sidra Amin walks out to bat at number 3 for Pakistan Women! Harmanpreet Kaur tosses the ball to Deepti Sharma who will share the attack from the other end.

OUT! KNOCKED HER OVER! Renuka Singh Thakur with the early strike for India! A duck for Gull Feroza. Renuka stays over the wicket and pulls her length back just a touch, on the off-stump line. With the keeper, Richa Ghosh coming up to the stumps for this ball, Gull Feroza is forced to stay in her crease. Tries to keep it out on the off side with an angled bat but does not account for the inward movement. The ball goes past the inside edge and crashes into the off pole. Pakistan Women lose one early and are 1/1 at the end of the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Renuka Singh Thakur to Gull Feroza, OUT! b Renuka Singh Thakur.

Commentary.Commentary: Renuka continues to shape the ball back into the right-hander, on off, Gull Feroza uses her feet to negate the movement and drives it along the carpet to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Renuka Singh Thakur to Gull Feroza, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and around off, swinging into the right-hander, Gull Feroza pats it with a straight bat down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Renuka Singh Thakur to Gull Feroza, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A loud shout but that seemed to be going down leg! Renuka thinks that it is going down leg but the keeper, Richa Ghosh looks interested. Harmanpreet Kaur decides against the review. Shaping back in sharply, full and on middle and leg, Gull Feroza looks to work it away with the swing on the leg side. Gets beaten on the inside edge and wears it on the front pad. The Ball Tracking shows the ball to be missing the leg stump. So, a wise decision by India not to go for the review.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Renuka Singh Thakur to Gull Feroza, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Muneeba Ali Siddiqi and Pakistan Women are off the mark! Sprayed on the pads by Renuka, on a fuller length, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi flicks it off her pads to the right of deep fine leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Renuka starts from over the wicket and attacks the stumps, shaping away a touch, on a length, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi gets behind the line and pushes it back to the bowler with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Renuka Singh Thakur to Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The pre-match formalities are complete, and it's time for the action to unfold! The umpires make their way to the middle followed closely by the Indian team, who gather for a final huddle before spreading across to take the field. Gull Feroza and Muneeba Ali Siddiqi are the openers for Pakistan Women. Renuka Singh Thakur has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for India Women. Away we go!

We are just moments away from the first ball in this thrilling blockbuster clash, which is also the 100th T20I at this prestigious venue! But before the action kicks off, the two captains, Harmanpreet Kaur and Fatima Sana Khan will proudly lead their teams onto the field for the national anthems. It will be Pakistan's national anthem first followed by India's national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Mel Jones is near the deck. She starts by saying that is very hot in Dubai with temperatures hovering around 37 degrees. Informs that we have moved two pitches across and pitch number 5 will be used for this game. Mentions that the dimensions of the square boundaries are 61 metres and 60 metres with the straight hit being 73 metres. Anjum Chopra joins her and says that batters will need to assess the conditions quickly here. Adds that it will be challenging for the batters with the surface being on the drier side. Anjum opines that batters will have to adjust their downswing while batting on this strip and looking at the grass covering, she feels that balls might hold up.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says she was also looking to bat first. Informs that Pooja Vastrakar misses out due to a niggle and Sajana Sajeevan comes in for her. Adds they are looking positively at the games to come. Ends by saying they just need to play some good cricket.

Fatima Sana Khan, the skipper of Pakistan Women says they want to try and put a good total on the board. Adds that they have one change in the side and Diana Baig is out and undergoing treatment. Talks about the match-up and says they are hoping to do well. Mentions that the pitch looks good and they are hopeful of putting up a good total.

Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Muneeba Ali Siddiqi (WK), Gull Feroza, Sidra Amin, Omaima Sohail, Nida Dar, Aliya Riaz, Fatima Sana Khan (C), Tuba Hassan, Nashra Sundhu, Sadia Iqbal, Syeda Aroob Shah (In for Diana Baig).

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Sajana Sajeevan (In for Pooja Vastrakar), Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Asha Sobhana, Renuka Singh Thakur.
TOSS - Pakistan Women have won the toss and they will BAT first.

India Women have historically dominated Pakistan Women in T20I's, holding a commanding 12-3 record, including a victory in their most recent clash at the Asia Cup. However, Pakistan seem poised to challenge India’s dominance this time, coming in with renewed strength and confidence. This perfectly sets the stage for a thrilling and fitting battle. Stick around to see how it all pans out as the toss and team news come to you shortly.

India Women, on the other hand, suffered a significant setback in their opening clash against New Zealand, with a lacklustre batting performance contributing to their defeat. This loss makes it crucial for India to bounce back strongly and put their best foot forward in this key encounter. Over the years, India's batting has been one of their biggest strengths, and there’s no doubt they have the firepower to turn things around. However, facing Pakistan’s fierce bowling attack, India will need to remain focused, seize critical moments, and ensure they capitalize on every opportunity to make a lasting impact in this high-pressure match.

Pakistan Women staged a remarkable comeback with the ball after their batters faltered in their opening clash against Sri Lanka, securing their first win of the tournament. That victory certainly would have boosted their confidence, and they will want to carry the momentum heading into this high-stakes clash. However, concerns still loom over their batting lineup, as the middle order has often been left to compensate for top-order lapses. Against a formidable Indian side, Pakistan’s batters will need to step up and deliver consistently throughout the innings. The spin attack, which wreaked havoc in their previous match, will once again be key to their strategy. They’ll shoulder much of the responsibility in trying to contain India’s potent batting lineup, which poses a serious challenge.

Hello and a warm welcome to one of the most eagerly awaited matchups of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, where arch-rivals India Women and Pakistan Women lock horns in match number 7. The anticipation is at an all-time high, and the excitement is palpable here at the iconic Dubai International Cricket Stadium. This fierce rivalry always delivers, and today’s battle is set to be no exception, with both teams ready to give it their all in what promises to be a cracker of a contest.
... MATCH DAY ...

The ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, 2024 is up and running and we have already been treated with a flurry of entertainment but it is only going to get multiplied manifolds as the Dubai International Cricket Stadium prepares itself to host the biggest rivalry of cricket. An Asian clash between two powerhouse teams. It’s India Women taking on the Pakistan Women in Match number 7 and it promises to be a crackerjack of a contest. Both teams enter this match with contrasting fortunes from their opening games. India swallowed an extremely bitter pill and suffered a disappointing defeat against New Zealand, exposing vulnerabilities in their batting lineup. The Women in Blue struggled to make an impact, with no batter crossing the 20-run mark and several falling to soft dismissals or poor shot selection. On the other hand, Pakistan Women come into the match with momentum, having secured a victory against the ascended Sri Lanka Women. Their win was particularly impressive as they successfully defended a below-par target of less than a run-a-ball. Talking about India Women first. Coming into this match, they would desperately want to address the batting vulnerabilities and make amends to their approach. Also, would aim towards improving on the lackadaisical fielding performance in their previous game. India's batting lineup boasts tremendous potential, spearheaded by the in-form Smriti Mandhana and the explosive Shafali Verma at the top of the order. Their primary objective will be to provide a solid foundation for the rest of the team to build upon. The onus is on skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and the middle order to step up and shoulder more responsibility, especially if the top order fails to fire. In the bowling department, India's pace trio of Pooja Vastrakar, Renuka Singh, and Arundhati Reddy needs to find their rhythm quickly. With conditions likely favoring spin, India has the luxury of several match-winning spinners in their ranks. The versatile Deepti Sharma adds significant value as a reliable all-rounder, capable of making crucial contributions with both bat and ball. The key for India will be to mentally reset after their opening defeat. They must approach this high-stakes encounter against Pakistan Women with a fresh mindset. Pakistan Women kicked off their campaign on a positive note, but there's still room for improvement as they face their arch-rivals. Their batting, a longstanding area of concern, requires urgent attention and enhancement. Fatima Sana Khan emerged as the standout performer in their opening fixture, delivering crucial contributions with both bat and ball. Her all-round prowess will be key once again, but Pakistan can't afford to rely solely on her 'sheroics'. The onus is on the top order to step up and provide substantial support to their captain. In the spin department, Pakistan boasts a wealth of options, and these could prove to be game-changers, especially if the conditions favor turn. However, the squad was dealt a blow, and Diana Baig was injured. Her doubtful participation leaves Pakistan with limited seam bowling options, potentially affecting their tactical flexibility. And lastly, talking about the head-to-head records, India Women lead this contest by 5-2 in the T20 World Cups and also won when these two last met in Cape Town in 2023. Will the Pakistan Women slightly better their record against their arch-rivals, or will India Women bounce back and get their first two points on the table? This Group A clash is surely going to be a box-office blockbuster. Which team do you think will win?
